headline: KSE-100 notches a third straight gain to 170,765.22 as Wall Street closes out a strong week, even as the 10-year Treasury yield hits a 19-year high near 5.17% and oil snaps back above $105 after Trump rejects Iran's Strait of Hormuz proposal
mood: Cautiously constructive locally · oil and Fed policy the swing factors into the new week

snapshot.label: Brent / WTI
snapshot.delta: ▼ Fri on truce hopes; Mon rebound ~$105.8 (EST.)

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Notches a Third Straight Gain
five_things.html: The KSE-100 added 266.28 points (+0.16%) on Friday to close at 170,765.22, its third consecutive positive session, after swinging between an intraday high of 171,159.73 and a low of 169,890.56. KSE-100 volume eased to 212.46 million shares while broader-market turnover fell to 482.76 million shares (from 759.97 million) on traded value of Rs19.28 billion, with 57 stocks advancing against 41 decliners and 2 unchanged. Commercial banks (+161.84 index points), OMCs (+55.64) and cement (+52.48) led, with HBL (+71.32), UBL (+37.69), BAFL (+34.81), BAHL (+34.36) and PSO (+27.53) the top individual contributors; PSO also confirmed a Rs10/share dividend alongside lower quarterly earnings. Technology & communication, power generation and pharmaceuticals lagged, dragged by MEBL (−56.63), FFC (−38.25) and HUBC (−21.44). Arif Habib's Ali Najib said the index "traded in both directions before ending on a flattish note ahead of the weekend." The Express Tribune and Mettis Global confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Closes Out a Strong Week
five_things.html: US equities finished Friday higher across the board: the S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow gained 478.64 points (+0.93%) to 51,828.62, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.5% to 27,068.72, with all three notching weekly gains as fresh tech optimism offset a bruising bond sell-off and easing oil prices into the close. Yahoo Finance and TheStreet confirm the closes.

The 10-year Treasury yield finished Friday at 5.17%, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year ended at 4.81%, as markets continued to price roughly a 70% chance of a further Fed hike at the 27-28 October FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish stance. Advisor Perspectives and Trading Economics confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Oil Snaps Back as Trump Rejects Iran's Hormuz Offer
five_things.html: Brent settled Friday at $104.32 and WTI at $92.41, both down roughly 2% on the session as hopes of a US-Iran truce briefly cut the war premium, but crude reversed sharply on Monday — Brent trading back near $105.76 (+1.4% EST.) and WTI near $94.10 (+1.8% EST.) — after President Trump confirmed he had rejected Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. EnergyNow and CNBC confirm.

five_things.chip: Gold Holds Near $4,280, Silver Leads the Complex
five_things.html: Gold edged up 0.12% to $4,280.19 and silver gained 0.33% to $64.04 on Friday, with silver outperforming as physical demand offset a yield-driven cap on the week's gains for the broader metals complex. USAGOLD and Kitco confirm the closes.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape stayed constructive: the KSE-100 logged a third straight gain, up 0.16% to 170,765.22, led by banks and OMCs even as breadth stayed narrow (57 advancers vs 41 decliners). The backdrop is dominated by the IMF's fourth EFF / third RSF review mission, led by Iva Petrova, which arrived in Islamabad on 23 September for a near two-week visit running into early October — examining fiscal performance (mostly on track but for a revenue shortfall) and flagging government intervention in wheat and sugar markets as a policy slippage, alongside the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 still before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue. August CPI held at 11.15% y/y, well above the SBP's 5-7% target band; the SBP kept its policy rate at 11.5% at its 14 September MPC, with 6-month KIBOR at 11.72/11.97% (bid/offer) as of 22 September. Successful completion of the review could unlock roughly $1 billion under the EFF and $200 million under the RSF by late November/early December. Dawn and Mettis Global confirm.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf non-oil momentum remains a bright spot against a fraught energy backdrop: Saudi Arabia's PMI held at a six-month high of 53.8 in August (from 53.1 in July), while the UAE's non-oil PMI hit 55.3 (from 52.7), its fastest pace since December 2024. That resilience is being tested again: President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, sending Brent back above $105 on Monday, while the region is still absorbing the fallout from Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi energy and industrial infrastructure earlier this month. OPEC+'s Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee holds its 68th meeting on 4 October to review production policy against constrained Gulf spare capacity, and Saudi's PIF continues executing its 2026-2030 strategy — approved by the Crown Prince in April — across travel & tourism, NEOM, advanced manufacturing and clean energy. Arab News and Al Jazeera confirm.
matrix.global_html: The dominant global theme stays the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield's climb to 5.17%, a 19-year high, reflects Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish path and October hike odds near 70% on CME-tracked pricing — yet Wall Street still closed out the week higher on fresh tech optimism. Crude is the other swing factor: Friday's dip on US-Iran truce hopes reversed Monday as Trump rejected Tehran's Hormuz-reopening proposal, pushing Brent back toward $106. Separately, Washington's tariff agenda widens on 29 September, when the 100% Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals and APIs extends to all remaining importers beyond the large firms already covered since July, with generics and biosimilars still exempt pending a mandated one-year review. Advisor Perspectives and Federal Register confirm.

legislative.policy_html: Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — remains with the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue as the IMF's 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission examines the proposed governance and disclosure amendments in Islamabad through early October
legislative.impact_html: Wins: institutional investors, IMF programme compliance, transparency advocates. Loses: SOE management facing tighter oversight, patronage-linked appointments.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+ Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (68th meeting), 4 October 2026 — to review Gulf production policy as the Strait of Hormuz remains contested after Trump's rejection of Iran's reopening proposal
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf producers with alternate export routes, non-oil diversification plays (tourism, construction) on resilient PMIs. Loses: export-constrained Gulf energy exporters absorbing Hormuz-linked shut-ins.

legislative.policy_html: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs — the 100% duty on patented drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients extends to all remaining importers from 29 September 2026, having applied to large Annex III companies since 31 July
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Annex III/onshoring pharma manufacturers with MFN pricing deals (exempt to 2029), generics and biosimilars (exempt pending review). Loses: mid-size and smaller branded importers newly facing the 100% duty.

levels.support_note: Friday's intraday low; deeper support at 168,700

desk_stance_html: The desk reads Friday's 0.16% gain as a continuation of the three-session recovery rather than a fresh breakout, with breadth narrowing (57 advancers vs 41 decliners) and volume thinning to 212 million shares as investors squared positions ahead of the weekend. The overnight and weekend tape complicates the open: Brent's reversal back toward $106 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal, alongside a 19-year-high 10-year Treasury yield and roughly 70% odds of an October Fed hike, argue for a cautious, energy- and rate-sensitive session. A close above 171,160 would extend the recovery toward Thursday's 172,491 high; a break below 169,900 opens room toward 168,700. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

US equities finished Friday higher across the board: S&P 500 +0.51% to 7,743.41, Dow +0.93% to 51,828.62, Nasdaq +0.5% to 27,068.72, all three posting weekly gains on fresh tech optimism. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.17%, its highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.81%, as markets price roughly 70% odds of an October Fed hike under Chair Kevin Warsh.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 added 266.28 points (+0.16%) to 170,765.22, a third consecutive positive session, on narrowing breadth (57 up, 41 down) as banks, OMCs and cement led (HBL, UBL, BAFL, BAHL, PSO) against declines in tech, power and pharma names (MEBL, FFC, HUBC). Volume eased to 212.46m shares on Rs19.28bn traded value; PSO confirmed a Rs10/share dividend alongside lower earnings. The IMF's fourth EFF / third RSF review mission, led by Iva Petrova, is in Islamabad through early October examining fiscal performance and the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill still before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue; wheat and sugar market intervention was flagged as a policy slippage. August CPI held at 11.15% y/y; the SBP kept its policy rate at 11.5% on 14 September; 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.72/11.97%.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's PMI held at a six-month high of 53.8 in August; the UAE's non-oil PMI hit 55.3, its fastest pace since December 2024 — both resilient even as Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, sending Brent back above $105 on Monday. The region is also absorbing the fallout from Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure earlier this month. OPEC+'s JMMC meets 4 October to review production policy, while PIF continues executing its 2026-2030 strategy across tourism, NEOM and advanced manufacturing.

GLOBAL
Brent settled Friday at $104.32 and WTI at $92.41, both down on brief US-Iran truce hopes, before reversing Monday to roughly $105.8/$94.1 (EST.) on Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz offer. Gold edged up 0.12% to $4,280.19 and silver gained 0.33% to $64.04. Washington's tariff agenda widens 29 September: the 100% Section 232 duty on patented pharmaceuticals and APIs extends to all remaining importers, having applied to large Annex III firms since 31 July; generics and biosimilars stay exempt pending a mandated one-year review.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
Pakistan: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill remains in Senate committee under IMF scrutiny — wins: institutional investors, IMF compliance; loses: SOE management facing tighter oversight.
GCC: OPEC+ JMMC meets 4 October amid renewed Hormuz tension — wins: non-oil diversification plays; loses: export-constrained Gulf energy exporters.
Global: Section 232 pharma tariff widens from 29 September — wins: onshoring pharma majors, generics; loses: mid-size branded importers newly exposed.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,900 (deeper support 168,700), pivot 170,765 (Friday's close), resistance 171,160 (then Thursday's 172,491 high). The desk reads Friday's move as a continuation of the three-session recovery rather than a breakout, with Monday's oil reversal, a 19-year-high 10-year yield and roughly 70% October hike odds arguing for a cautious, rate- and energy-sensitive session.
